A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ObjectMLLM and contain readable main texts, figures, tables, and complete appendices. The original experiments and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original video-QA experiments on five benchmarks, including adapter comparisons, modality ablations, fine-tuning results, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds BABEL-QA human-motion experiments, temporal-sampling sensitivity results, and spatial-free-caption experiments.

M1.justification: Section 4.7 extends the existing language interface to named 3D human joints, serializing six sampled poses with coordinates normalized to integers in [0, 1000]. This is a limited input adaptation beyond v1's bounding boxes. The original detection, tracking, box adapters, and fine-tuning procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds BABEL-QA, extending evaluation to a distinct human-motion setting with 3D joint trajectories and rendered pose videos. This substantively broadens the represented data and structured-input coverage beyond object bounding boxes. All five original video-QA benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds the LLaMA3 video-plus-box configuration to the main modality comparison; v1 reported this configuration for Perception Test in Appendix Table A9. The external MLLM comparator set in Table 4 remains LLaVA-Next-Video-DPO, VideoLLaMA2, SeViLA, ViLA, and Vamos.

E3.justification: The original benchmark settings are retained. Added experiments introduce 50-epoch BABEL-QA training, CLEVRER-MC box sampling at 0.25–2 FPS, Perception Test box-token budgets of 600–1200, and a GPT-4o caption-generation protocol that excludes spatial information. These are extensions of the evaluation design.

E4.justification: V2 adds temporal-sampling sensitivity analysis in Appendix B.4/Table A7 and tests spatial-free captions with and without boxes in Appendix C/Table A8. Table 1 also expands the modality ablation. Existing projector, object-label, fusion, tracking-quality, and failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report accuracy values and learning curves without disclosed repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The added experiments retain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 substantially expands the findings with BABEL-QA results: 66.6 video, 60.2 caption, 63.5 pose, 68.6 video-plus-pose, and 69.4 caption-plus-pose accuracy. It also adds sampling and spatial-free-caption results and four previously unreported LLaMA3 video-plus-box benchmark scores. Perception Test's 62.7 already appeared in v1 Table A9. Matched original results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs. The added pose serialization and sampling experiments do not introduce a new mathematical argument or formal guarantee.

C1.justification: V2's introduction and conclusion add an experimentally supported claim that ObjectMLLM generalizes to richer structured representations, specifically human poses. The central claims about explicit object information and the data efficiency of language-based representations remain.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly discusses lossy coordinate quantization and computational cost, interprets sampling results as an accuracy-efficiency trade-off, and adds an interpretation of spatial information's limited role on NExT-QA and IntentQA. Existing limitations concerning appearance, actions, training coverage, and annotation bias are retained.

D1.justification: V1 promises a future code/model release; v2 states that they are released and supplies project and repository addresses. V2 also documents binary search for the existing box-token limit, pose preprocessing, and BABEL-QA training duration. The binary-search description is newly disclosed detail, without evidence that the original sampling procedure changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Endo et al.'s motion-question-answering work for BABEL-QA and MoReVQA for caption-based reasoning. The broader research positioning remains stable. Consolidated duplicate references and publication-metadata updates do not constitute removed or newly introduced research.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial introduction and method passages, conclusion, and appendix explanations undergo extensive rewriting. Terminology shifts toward object-centric representations. Downsampling documentation moves into Appendix A.2, existing ablations move from C to B, and the new spatial-information analysis occupies C.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the opening bag illustration with a basketball example, adds Table 5, Tables A7–A8, and a caption-comparison Figure A2, and expands Table 1. V1 Figure 6 moves to v2 Figure A5. The existing pipeline diagrams, quantitative plots, and qualitative cases are largely retained within the same visual design.

improvement.justification: The human-pose evaluation, sampling analysis, clearer explanations, and additional reproducibility information provide useful support and transparency. Appendix C's evidential benefit is limited because it changes both captioner and spatial content. These gains outweigh a localized new overstatement: Section 4.4 claims consistent video-plus-box improvements, although Table 1 reports STAR accuracy of 59.3 versus 59.7 for video alone.
